diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the original pipeline likely selected the first regex-matching date-like token (or an OCR-corrupted near-label like “Data:”) rather than prioritizing the primary header Date field. Dense invoices can contain multiple plausible dd/mm(/yyyy) strings; without label/context ranking, the wrong one is chosen.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true. Source-run evidence shows competing header-adjacent date-like strings due to OCR label corruption (DATE→DATA) and multiple header fields. The atif_steps and related OCR snippets show that the extraction logic returned the first match without ranking, which is brittle on invoices like 034.jpg.

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure due to OCR digit-flip outlier and over-trusting a single TOTAL-like line. The receipt contains multiple internal anchors (Subtotal/Payment/Total incl) consistent with one value, but OCR produced a conflicting outlier (e.g., 102.00→702.00) on a later TOTAL-like line; naive “last TOTAL wins” or keyword-tier priority without anchor override selects the outlier.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=702.00. Source-run OCR snippets show both anchors (“Subtotal : 102.00”, “Payment : 102.00”, “Total incl. of GST 102.00”) and an outlier “Total ... 702.00” / “Total Amt Rounded ... 702.00”. This is a classic OCR 1→7 digit flip where internal consistency should override a single corrupted line.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: the receipt shows an inclusive total, a rounding adjustment, then a final payable TOTAL. The pipeline selected the pre-rounding inclusive total instead of the final total after rounding, causing an exact-match miss (often by 0.01).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=23.26. The image shows “Rounding Adj: -0.01” followed by bold “TOTAL: 23.25”, while an earlier line shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”. This requires an unconditional precedence rule: if rounding adjustment exists and a later TOTAL exists, take the later TOTAL.

diagnoses.description: Schema/normalization failure plus header-triggered fallback risk: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null. Additionally, this receipt contains an “Amount” column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may also corrupt the GRAND TOTAL keyword and decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates task requirement (must be null on failure). Source-run trace shows matching on “Description Qty Price Amount” and split-line fallback to an item amount; OCR variants include “GrandTota.” and “92:80”. Even if extraction fails, output must be null, never empty string.

quality_impact.rationale: No skill edits proposed because the current candidate image-ocr SKILL.md already documents the missing behaviors evidenced in the source run (header/label-tolerant date ranking; anchor-consistency override; rounding precedence; header-line exclusion; decimal-separator normalization; and empty-string→null guard). The dominant gap in the historical run is implementation adherence (first-match date, last-match total, weak fallback gating), not missing guidance.

trigger_precision.rationale: By not broadening heuristics further, we avoid regressions. The candidate’s existing rules are already tightly gated (e.g., split-line fallback only when keyword line has no digits and is not a header; anchor override only when multiple anchors agree; optional upscaling only as fallback).

instruction_compliance.rationale: Diagnoses use only permitted evidence (field-level correctness feedback, predictions, and provided OCR snippets/images). No oracle values are referenced. No tool execution is requested. No unnecessary skill files are modified.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Diagnoses cover all four incorrect fields and connect them to concrete failure mechanisms visible in the source run (first-match date; last-match total; missing rounding precedence; missing schema guard; header-triggered fallback). The current candidate skill already covers these mechanisms.

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The historical failures are explained by simplistic selection/normalization in the original implementation (first regex date; last TOTAL-like line; split-line fallback triggering on headers; no anchor/rounding precedence enforcement; empty-string output). The current candidate image-ocr skill already encodes the minimal, transferable heuristics needed to prevent these errors. Therefore, this iteration recommends no further SKILL.md changes; the next improvement would be ensuring downstream implementations follow the documented rules.
